ABOUT THE ROLE:

The best SDETs in the industry are no longer measured by how many tests they write. They're measured by the systems they build that decide whether software is safe to ship — and, increasingly, by how well they wield AI to do it.



That's the role we're hiring for. We're looking for a Senior Staff SDET to own quality architecture and engineering strategy for our most critical systems, and to lead how we apply AI across our entire testing and release pipeline. You'll build the frameworks, platforms, and agent-driven workflows that the rest of engineering depends on, define what "safe to ship" means here, and stay deep in the code while doing it.



This is a genuinely hands-on senior technical leadership role with impact that spans many teams. If you want to build AI-native quality systems rather than bolt AI tools onto a legacy suite, this is that job.




WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

 - AI is the core of the work. You'll own how we use LLMs and agents for test generation, failure triage, self-healing, and release decisioning — and you'll set the guardrails that keep it trustworthy.

 - You'll test AI, not just test with it. We ship AI-powered product features, which means building evaluation harnesses, golden datasets, and probabilistic assertions for systems that don't return the same answer twice. This is frontier work with very little established playbook.

 - Real autonomy and real scope. You'll set the technical direction for quality engineering, not inherit someone else's strategy.




YOU WILL:

Own quality architecture and strategy

 - Own quality architecture for our most critical systems and initiatives, defining long-term quality strategy aligned with business and product goals.

 - Design shared quality platforms, automation frameworks, and test infrastructure that are adopted across multiple teams.

 - Establish quality patterns and guardrails that scale across teams, eliminating duplicated, brittle, or low-signal testing approaches through platform-level solutions.

 - Anticipate systemic quality and reliability risks and drive preventative architectural solutions before they impact customers.

 - Set the standard for what "great" looks like in quality engineering at scale.

Lead our AI-driven testing strategy

 - Define and drive our strategy for AI-assisted testing — autonomous test generation, intelligent test selection, agent-based failure triage, and self-healing automation — with a clear-eyed view of where each genuinely pays off and where it adds noise.

 - Build the guardrails that make AI-driven testing trustworthy: knowing when a self-healing agent is masking a real regression versus absorbing harmless implementation drift is the difference between leverage and liability.

 - Orchestrate AI agents as part of the CI/CD decision pipeline, turning raw test signal into release confidence rather than more dashboards.

 - Own quality for our AI-powered product features — designing eval suites, golden datasets, LLM-as-judge scorers, and statistical approaches for non-deterministic behavior, plus testing for hallucination, safety, and response stability.

 - Establish how we test AI-generated application code, validating behavioral correctness and not just syntactic plausibility.

 - Evaluate emerging AI testing tooling with real rigor, and be honest about what doesn't work.

Raise the bar operationally and across the team

 - Lead the operational maturity of our quality systems and signals — defining quality metrics, dashboards, and release confidence indicators, and leading post-incident analysis that informs architectural and process improvements.

 - Produce exemplary technical artifacts — quality architecture documents, automation frameworks, test platforms — that set the bar for the rest of the team, while staying hands-on in critical quality systems and automation code paths.

 - Serve as the accountable technical leader for strategic initiatives, proactively managing reliability, scalability, and technical debt across teams.

 - Mentor senior SDETs, quality engineers, and other senior technical leaders — especially on building AI fluency into their practice.

 - Establish hiring standards, coaching, and talent development.

 - Champion customer-centric quality decisions, ensuring technical trade-offs reflect real user needs and long-term product value.

 - Partner with Engineering and Product leadership to embed scalability and resilience into roadmap planning, not just technical design.




YOU HAVE:

 - 10+ years of hands-on experience in quality engineering or SDET roles, including experience architecting quality strategy and automation platforms across multiple teams.

 - Proven track record designing and scaling test automation frameworks across the full stack — frontend web, mobile, and backend/API (e.g., Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, Appium, Postman, or similar).

 - Deep proficiency in one or more programming languages (e.g., JavaScript, TypeScript, Kotlin) used to build and maintain shared automation frameworks and tooling. You write production-quality code, not just test scripts.

 - Hands-on experience applying AI to testing — LLM-assisted test generation, agent-based workflows, intelligent test selection, or self-healing automation — with informed opinions about where it delivers and where it disappoints.

 - Demonstrated ability to define quality architecture and standards that scale across many teams, including shared quality platforms and test infrastructure.

 - Strong grasp of modern development and delivery practices (agile/lean, DevOps, shift-left testing, TDD) and experience embedding quality gates into CI/CD systems (e.g., GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Jenkins).

 - Experience mentoring and developing senior quality engineers and senior technical leaders, with a track record of raising the technical bar across a group or organization.

 - History of leading post-incident and root-cause analysis that drives architectural and process change.

 - Excellent judgment on trade-offs between short-term delivery and long-term system resilience and maintainability.

 - Strong executive communication skills, with the ability to influence engineering and product leadership on quality strategy, risk, and investment.

 - Experience with performance and load testing at scale.




NICE TO HAVE:

 - Familiarity with LLM observability and evaluation tooling (e.g., Braintrust, Arize, MLflow, LangSmith, or similar).

 - Experience with cloud-based testing platforms and tools (e.g., AWS Device Farm, Sauce Labs, BrowserStack).

 - Familiarity with e-commerce or healthcare platforms and quality-at-scale practices in regulated environments.

 - Experience with internationalization and localization testing.

 - A track record of building quality engineering communities of practice — tech talks, katas, lunch-and-learns.

 - Published writing, talks, or open-source work on modern testing practice or AI in quality engineering.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a highly motivated, detail-oriented Manager, Production Planning to lead the planning team responsible for our non-sterile compounded production. This position manages and develops the site's production planners and owns the forward-looking production plan. The plan converts demand forecasts and inventory policy into a rolling view of the next several weeks through the next year or more, tests that plan against labor, equipment, and material capacity, and identifies where the business cannot meet it. The Manager then drives the response to each gap, whether through training, labor, or capital investment, and hands the plan to Production Scheduling for on-site execution. The ideal candidate is a proactive people leader with a strong understanding of integrated planning systems, supply chain dynamics, and cross-functional collaboration across the operations planning team.

 


YOU WILL:

 - Lead, manage, and develop the team of production planners, setting priorities, coaching, reviewing output, and ensuring consistent planning practices and coverage.

 - Own the development and maintenance of mid- and long-term production plans for non-sterile compounded products in alignment with demand forecasts and inventory policies.

 - Define the planning horizons, plan-of-record cadence, and frozen window, and publish the plan to Production Scheduling on a fixed schedule.

 - Manage finished goods inventory for compounded products within company guidance while maintaining click-to-deliver metrics for customers.

 - Develop what-if scenarios that identify where and when the plan exceeds available capacity, and which constraints are most sensitive to demand, product mix, batch size, and shift patterns.

 - Articulate and document all risks resulting from production capacity constraints, including volume at risk, timing, and effect on delivery and inventory. If the plan cannot be met, make or recommend revisions when plans cannot be met, and document the reason for each revision.

 - Recommend and size actions to close each gap, including training and cross-training for skill coverage, hiring and labor planning, overtime and shift design, equipment and facility investment, and outsourcing. Partner with Compounding Operations, HR, and Quality to carry out approved actions and track whether each one delivers the capacity it was sized to deliver.

 - Monitor plan attainment, forecast accuracy, and capacity utilization at the weekly and monthly level, analyze variances, and implement corrective actions.

 - Use actual cycle times, yields, and throughput reported by Production Scheduling to update planning standards and capacity model assumptions.

 - Collaborate cross-functionally across the operations planning team, partnering with demand planning to communicate forecast discrepancies and agree on the plan of record, with production scheduling to confirm the plan can be executed and take in the constraints it escalates, and with procurement and raw materials planning to confirm material availability.

 - Develop and maintain tools, dashboards, and KPIs that communicate plan status, constraints, risks, and performance to plan to leadership.

 


YOU HAVE:

 - 8+ years experience in at least 1 of the following: Production planning, capacity planning, or resource planning, with demonstrated experience leading or developing others.

 - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Industrial Engineering, or related field required; APICS/CPIM certification a plus.

 - Experience building capacity models and presenting investment, staffing, or outsourcing recommendations to senior leaders.

 - Proficient in inventory management concepts with an understanding of the financial and operational implications of planning decisions.

 - Experience in pharmaceutical or pharmacy production/manufacturing environments is a plus.

 - Excel proficiency including experience with data manipulations – Lookups, PivotTables, External Data Connections.

 - Basic SQL and/or Python experience is a plus.

 - Deep knowledge of supply chain and manufacturing planning processes.

 - Strong analytical skills and comfort with data-driven decision making.

 - Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

 - Ability to manage multiple priorities and lead a team in a fast-paced environment.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Hims & Hers is scaling a multi-site sterile and nonsterile manufacturing network spanning 503A compounding pharmacies, a 503B outsourcing facility, and a peptide active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing site. The Manager, Technical Services is the site-level technical owner responsible for executing process verification, cleaning validation, and technology transfer activities, driving process optimization, and resolving equipment and process issues at their assigned facility. This role reports to the Director, Technical Services and works closely with site Operations, Quality, Engineering, and Maintenance to keep manufacturing running reliably day to day, while supporting process development, capital equipment installation, equipment qualification, and requalification work as the site grows.

 


YOU WILL:

Process Verification

 - Execute process verification activities for compounded preparations and manufacturing processes at the site, confirming that critical process parameters and in-process controls are consistently met.

 - Author and execute process verification protocols and reports, and maintain supporting data packages for audit and inspection readiness.

 - Flag process drift or emerging trends to site leadership and the Director, Technical Services, and recommend corrective action.

 - At sterile sites, plan and execute site-level aseptic process simulations (media fills) in line with network standards set by the Director, Technical Services, and support any related investigations.

Cleaning Validation

 - Execute the site's cleaning validation program, including cleaning method verification, swab and rinse sampling, and acceptance limit checks for compounding, filling, and processing equipment.

 - Author and execute cleaning validation protocols and reports, and manage the ongoing cleaning verification/monitoring schedule for the site.

 - Assess the cleaning validation impact of new products, equipment changes, or campaign changes at the site, and escalate revalidation needs to the Director, Technical Services.

Tech Transfer

 - Support and execute technology transfer of new products, formulations, and processes into the site, including transfers from R&D or from other manufacturing sites.

 - Coordinate site-level activities against transfer protocols, ensuring critical process parameters and acceptance criteria are met during transfer runs.

 - Partner with R&D, Quality, and Operations to document a smooth, well-supported transition from transfer to routine commercial production at the site.

Process Optimization

 - Identify and lead site-level continuous improvement projects to increase process robustness, throughput, and consistency.

 - Analyze process and yield data to identify optimization opportunities, and implement changes through the site's change control process.

 - Partner with Operations to translate optimization initiatives into standard work and operator training updates.

Equipment Troubleshooting

 - Serve as the site's first-line technical resource for diagnosing and resolving equipment performance issues, breakdowns, or unexpected results on compounding, filling, sterilization, or API processing equipment.

 - Partner with site Engineering and Maintenance to identify equipment-related root causes and implement fixes that restore or improve reliability.

 - Support commissioning and start-up troubleshooting for new or upgraded equipment during site qualification and launch phases.

Process Investigations

 - Lead or support root-cause investigations for process-related deviations, yield losses, and quality issues at the site.

 - Drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to closure, and verify effectiveness of implemented changes.

 - Maintain clear, defensible investigation documentation suitable for internal review and regulatory inspection.

Regulatory Inspection Support

 - Participate in FDA and state board of pharmacy inspections as the site's technical subject matter expert, providing front-room or back-room support as needed.

 - Respond to inspector questions and provide documentation on process verification, cleaning validation, technology transfer, and troubleshooting history for the site, and support technical responses to observations tied to process, cleaning, or equipment performance.

Team Leadership

 - Lead, coach, and develop the site's Technical Services team, setting clear priorities and holding the team accountable for quality, timeliness, and safety of their work.

 - Own hiring, onboarding, performance management, and career development for direct reports, in partnership with HR.

 - Plan team workload and capacity across process verification, cleaning validation, tech transfer, and troubleshooting activities to meet site production and compliance timelines.

 - Build technical capability on the team through training, mentorship, and knowledge-sharing on validation practices and equipment troubleshooting.

In addition to the primary responsibilities above, this role provides site-level support for the following:

 - Process Development — supporting scale-up and process definition activities for new products transitioning from R&D to the site.

 - Capital Install — supporting installation and startup activities for new capital equipment, including coordination with Engineering and vendors.

 - Equipment IOQ/PQ — supporting Installation, Operational, and Performance Qualification execution for new or upgraded equipment.

 - Requalification — supporting periodic requalification of equipment and processes per site schedules and change control triggers.


YOU HAVE:

 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Pharmacy, Chemistry, or a related technical/scientific field required.

 - 5+ years of experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing or sterile/nonsterile compounding, with hands-on experience in process verification, cleaning validation, technology transfer, or equipment troubleshooting.

 - Prior experience supervising or leading technical staff, including hiring, coaching, and performance management, in a regulated manufacturing or compounding environment.

 - Working knowledge of USP <795>, <797>, and <800> (as applicable to site), FDA's Process Validation Guidance (2011), and cGMP requirements.

 - Experience supporting root-cause investigations and CAPA in a regulated manufacturing environment.

 - Strong technical writing skills, with the ability to author clear, defensible protocols and reports.

 - Comfort working hands-on with manufacturing equipment and collaborating cross-functionally with Operations, Quality, and Engineering.

 


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with peptide, oligonucleotide, or other complex API manufacturing processes.

 - Hands-on experience with autoclaves, isolators, filling lines, or API processing/purification equipment.

 - Experience supporting new equipment commissioning, IOQ/PQ execution, or site launch activities.

 - Prior experience supporting FDA or state board of pharmacy inspections.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Operations Manager leads day-to-day peptide manufacturing operations at our cGMP facility across both upstream operations, including solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) synthesis & cleavage, and downstream operations, including preparative HPLC purification, lyophilization, and final packaging. You will ensure operations are executed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with cGMP, and you will own the full process from resin to final packaged peptide.

This is a hands-on leadership role reporting directly to the Site Head, with authority over manufacturing staffing, scheduling, and operational performance. The CGMP Manufacturing Supervisors, Production Chemists, and Production Technicians roll up to this role. You will work cross-functionally with Quality, Supply Chain, Planning, Engineering, and MSAT/Process Development to deliver production schedules, improve operational performance, and maintain a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement. Experience in both upstream and downstream operations is required for this role.

This role is based in Menlo Park, CA at our H&H Peptides facility.




YOU WILL:

Manufacturing Operations:

 - Lead daily upstream and downstream manufacturing activities to ensure safe, compliant, and efficient execution of production campaigns.

 - Manage staffing, scheduling, and production priorities across synthesis, cleavage, purification, and lyophilization to meet business objectives.

 - Monitor and drive performance metrics, including safety, schedule attainment, throughput, yield, and right-first-time execution.

 - Maintain a strong floor presence and provide hands-on operational leadership and support.

Upstream Oversight (SPPS & Cleavage):

 - Oversee daily SPPS and cleavage operations, including resin preparation, coupling and deprotection cycles, cleavage, precipitation, and isolation of crude peptide.

 - Ensure upstream execution adheres to approved batch records, SOPs, and process parameters, including safe handling of hazardous solvents and reagents.

Downstream Oversight (Purification & Lyophilization):

 - Oversee prep HPLC purification, fraction pooling, lyophilization, final isolation, and packaging operations, and support troubleshooting of prep and analytical HPLC operations.

 - Ensure downstream execution adheres to approved batch records, SOPs, and process parameters, and coordinate with QC on in-process and release testing.

 - Ensure a smooth hand-off of crude peptide from upstream to downstream to keep campaigns on schedule.

Troubleshooting & Equipment:

 - Support troubleshooting of manufacturing processes, equipment, and production issues.

 - Support equipment qualification, preventive maintenance, and facility readiness in coordination with Engineering and Maintenance.

Process Improvement:

 - Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, productivity, throughput, and cost reduction.

 - Identify process bottlenecks and implement solutions to improve manufacturing performance.

 - Use Lean Manufacturing principles and data-driven decision making to optimize operations.

 - Partner with MSAT/Process Development and Quality on technology transfer, process validation, scale-up, and process improvement initiatives.

Quality & Compliance:

 - Keep manufacturing operations inspection-ready and compliant with cGMP (21 CFR 210/211, ICH Q7), including ALCOA+ and 21 CFR Part 11 data integrity.

 - Support deviations, root cause investigations, effective CAPAs, change controls, and audit and inspection activities, including responses and follow-up commitments.

 - Promote a culture of quality and right-first-time execution.

People Leadership:

 - Coach, develop, and lead manufacturing supervisors, leads, chemists, operators, and technicians across upstream and downstream; set clear expectations and performance metrics.

 - Support hiring, onboarding, GMP training, and performance management, and ensure training matrices, cross-training, and shift coverage are maintained.

 - Participate in production planning and operational review meetings.




YOU HAVE:

 - 2+ years of supervisory or people leadership experience in a GMP-regulated manufacturing environment.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Hims & Hers is looking for a dependable, detail-oriented R&D Sterile Compounding Technician to support sterile product development. Working alongside our formulation scientists, you will prepare development and feasibility batches, execute experimental protocols in controlled environments, and capture the high-quality data that moves new sterile products forward.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys iterating and troubleshooting while respecting the discipline of GMP, aseptic technique, and approved protocols.



Hours: 

Standard Hours: Typically 7:00 AM – 3:30 PM.

 - Flexibility Required: Must be available for occasional early starts or late finishes (window of 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM) based on production mixes, business needs, and travel.




YOU WILL:

 - Prepare and compound sterile development, feasibility, and engineering batches according to approved protocols, SOPs, and batch records.

 - Perform dilution, concentration, and gravimetric/volumetric calculations accurately and verify them as required.

 - Operate and maintain laboratory and process equipment, including balances, pH meters, mixers, filtration systems, pumps, and semi-automated and automated filling equipment.

 - Perform aseptic processing, filtration, and filling in ISO 5-8 environments, including material transfer and in-process visual inspection of units for foreign matter.

 - Perform routine compounding operations, including measuring, compounding, and sterilizing labware and solutions, and verify steps as required.

 - Label, package, and ship development and feasibility samples in accordance with approved procedures.

 - Execute experimental plans, adapting technique as results change, within defined protocol boundaries.

 - Document all work in real time in lab notebooks, batch records, and Excel, following data integrity principles (ALCOA+). Complete controlled documents and assignments right the first time, with minimal errors and within the required timeline.

 - Promptly report unexpected results, deviations, and improvement ideas to the formulation scientist or supervisor through proper channels, rather than working around them. Support continuous improvement efforts.

 - Identify, communicate, troubleshoot, and help implement solutions for problems noticed in the cleanroom or during critical processes.

 - Assemble and organize experimental data and communicate status to R&D and cross-functional partners (Quality, Manufacturing, Analytical). Collaborate across teams to keep projects moving.

 - Prepare, clean, sterilize, and depyrogenate labware and equipment; clean and maintain cleanroom equipment; keep cleanroom suites and support areas organized and inspection-ready.

 - Complete required training (GMP, aseptic technique, safety) and maintain gowning and aseptic qualifications (e.g., media fill, gloved fingertip sampling), working within your qualified scope.

 - Step in flexibly as priorities and timelines shift, and help meet batch schedules and project targets.




YOU HAVE:

 - High school diploma or equivalent; [Associate’s/Bachelor’s in a scientific field] preferred.

 - Experience in a sterile compounding, pharmaceutical cleanroom, GMP, or laboratory formulation setting.

 - Strong aseptic technique, garbing, and cleanroom behavior.

 - Proficiency with pharmaceutical calculations (dilutions, concentrations, unit conversions).

 - Meticulous documentation habits and understanding of data integrity.

 - Deep understanding of why sterility matters, and of the differences between mechanical cleaning, sanitization, disinfection, and sterilization.

 - Hands-on experience with laboratory and process equipment (balances, pH meters, mixers, filtration, pumps).

 - Ability to work independently, understand objectives, and ask clarifying questions early to meet production and project targets with minimal supervision.

 - Strong organizational and communication skills.

 - Ability to stand for extended periods and work in gowned, controlled environments.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 1+ years of sterile compounding, cleanroom manufacturing, or pharmaceutical lab experience.

 - Working knowledge of USP <797>/<800>, cGMP, and GDP.

 - Experience with needle/syringe manipulation; media fill and gloved fingertip sampling qualification history.

 - Experience operating semi-automated or automated filling machines.




WHAT MAKES YOU SUCCESSFUL:

 - Experimental mindset: you troubleshoot proactively and treat unexpected results as information.

 - Calm and deliberate under pressure.

 - Self-directed but not unilateral: you act with a clear understanding of requirements and seek guidance when unsure. You are comfortable being wrong and unafraid to ask.

 - Organized and collaborative: you keep work tidy inside and outside the cleanroom and communicate clearly across teams.

 - Self-motivated and proactive: you notice problems early, raise them, and help solve them.

 - Dependable: teammates can count on you to follow SOPs and batch records exactly and to step in when needed.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Senior Manager, Maintenance leads the maintenance and reliability function for a GMP peptide manufacturing facility, providing high-level support to the Site Operations and Engineering organization through predictive and preventive maintenance programs for all production, utility, and facility equipment. This position analyzes, troubleshoots, and communicates maintenance problems and concerns in the following areas: electrical, mechanical, plumbing, compressed air and process gases, HVAC, and clean utilities, as they relate to equipment and controlled environments in the facility. The Senior Manager works with general supervision and will interact with the Site Lead regularly to receive guidance and feedback. Many non-routine activities will require the Site Lead’s advance approval.




YOU WILL:

 - Lead a group of maintenance technicians, supervisors, and managers across a multi-shift, multi-discipline operation.

 - Own the predictive and preventive maintenance program for all GMP equipment, including peptide synthesizers, preparative HPLC and purification systems, lyophilizers, filtration and TFF skids, reactors, isolators and hoods, autoclaves, and associated controls.

 - Maintain and reliably operate facility and clean utilities, including HVAC and cleanroom environmental systems, purified water/WFI, clean steam, compressed air, nitrogen and other process gases, and chilled and hot water systems.

 - Document maintenance, technical, and other data on predictive/preventive maintenance charts, as required.

 - Diagnose and repair equipment and systems throughout the facility, including electrical, mechanical, plumbing, compressed air, PLC/controls, and HVAC repairs.

 - Identify facility and equipment issues and develop an ongoing strategy to chart trends and take remedial action using a predictive maintenance approach.

 - Communicate to management all issues that could result in safety risks, product quality impact, or loss to Hims or its associates.

 - Work as directed in all areas of the facility to maintain safety and health standards.

 - Perform and oversee calibration and testing procedures on equipment to ensure accurate operation and compliance with quality standards.

 - Conduct regular checks and measurements to verify equipment performance, including temperature, pressure, speed, and other relevant parameters.

 - Maintain calibration records and documentation in compliance with cGMP and other regulatory requirements.

 - Ensure that all equipment meets regulatory and quality standards and take corrective actions to address any non-compliance issues.

 - Collaborate with Quality Assurance, Validation, and Regulatory Affairs to implement and maintain proper documentation, including equipment logs, maintenance records, change controls, deviations/CAPAs, and qualification and validation reports.

 - Support equipment and facility qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), commissioning, and requalification activities, and maintain the validated state of equipment through the change control process.

 - Respond promptly to equipment breakdowns, emergencies, and production interruptions to minimize downtime.

 - Work closely with production personnel to coordinate repairs and planned maintenance and minimize disruptions to the manufacturing schedule.

 - Develop and manage the maintenance budget, spare parts strategy, and external contractor and vendor relationships.

 - Identify opportunities for process optimization, efficiency improvements, and cost savings related to equipment maintenance and operation.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Production Technician supports hands-on cGMP peptide manufacturing, working in either upstream operations (synthesis and cleavage) or downstream operations (preparative HPLC purification and lyophilization). You will execute assigned batch record steps and accurately record the values and observations from each activity, safely and on schedule. Each day you will be assigned to either upstream or downstream activities, and cross-training in the other area may follow once you are established in the role. Experience in both areas is not required; experience in either one is enough.

This role reports to the Supervisor, CGMP Manufacturing. Recent graduates and entry-level candidates are encouraged to apply; training will be provided.

 This role is based in Menlo Park, CA at our H&H Peptides facility.




YOU WILL:

Execution:

 - Execute assigned manufacturing steps per approved batch records, SOPs, and work instructions, following each procedure exactly and in a timely, efficient manner.

 - Read work orders and batch records thoroughly, and understand the instructions and final product specifications before starting each task.

 - Upstream: assist with SPPS and cleavage operations, including resin preparation, synthesizer setup and operation, cleavage, precipitation, and crude peptide isolation.

 - Upstream: verify protected amino acids batch by batch against specification, including solubility and appearance, before use, and record the results.

 - Downstream: assist with prep HPLC purification, fraction collection and pooling, concentration, lyophilization, and final packaging.

 - Downstream: run analytical HPLC and mass checks on dissolved crude peptide as directed, and record the results for chemist review.

 - Handle raw materials, solvents, and reagents safely; operate and clean production equipment and instruments (such as HPLCs, centrifuges, freeze dryers, stir plates, laboratory balances, mass spectrometers, sonicators, vacuum ovens, and nitrogen supply) and report issues promptly.

 - Prepare and label chemical solutions and buffers according to standard formulas.

 - Perform in-process checks as specified in the batch record, record the values obtained, and escalate unexpected or out-of-range results right away.

Schedule Adherence:
